analysis.title: Tech Wrecked Again As AI Credit Cracks Widen; Doves & Diesel Battle Over Bonds
key_insights: Tech stocks lagged on Oct 13: SPX finished unchanged, NDX weak. AI-linked stocks fell, NeoClouds were the worst performers, and Mag7 outperformed NDX for 8 straight sessions.

Oil, yields and stocks recoupled after bonds reopened (US Treasuries were closed for Columbus Day). Oil rebounded from overnight lows on doubts over a Ukraine-Russia deal, no resolution in Hormuz, and the escalating Houthi-Saudi war, including a Saudi-coalition warning to evacuate a fuel station in Sanaa.

Diesel cracks have surged toward $100 and dirty tanker freight rates are at multi-year extremes. Bloomberg's Frank Monkam says this leaves Brent vulnerable to a catch-up move, which would lift bond vol, yields and inflation fears.

Russia struck Ukrainian power plants after Trump said both sides had agreed to stop targeting energy infrastructure. Zelensky accused Moscow of breaking the energy ceasefire, and diesel prices surged.
OPEC cut its 2026 oil demand growth forecast to about 400,000 bpd from 1.4 million bpd earlier in the year. OPEC+ production recovered in September, led by Saudi Arabia.
Axios reported that Netanyahu and Trump discussed a possible new operation against Iran before the Israeli and U.S. elections. WTI hit its highs of the day on the report.

Fed speakers were mixed. Goolsbee said rates can fall if inflation is on a path to 2%, but is increasingly nervous about overheating demand from AI. Barkin said the Fed can see AI investment's impact on inflation. Williams still sees one more hike this year and no need for more in 2027. Waller said higher yields are 'doing a little bit of the work'.
Dec hike odds rose to cycle highs near 90% and September odds returned to about 25%. CPI is due Oct 14.

The curve was mixed with the short end underperforming (30Y -3bps). 2s30s flattened to two-week lows. Bond vol is easing but remains decoupled from equity vol, so the next rates reversal may need an equity drawdown to come first.
IG and HY spreads both widened. Bloomberg's Michael Ball says the AI debate is shifting from compute demand to whether investors will keep financing the buildout at acceptable returns.

AI credit stress: JPMorgan and Goldman are leading a roughly $5B loan for AI startup Volta at about 11% but underwrote only $1.3B. CoreWeave debt trades near 85 cents on the dollar (about a 14% yield). Citi says 5-year CDS for megacap tech has tripled to about 75bps in a year. AI-linked capital raises have been delayed or canceled, and Broadcom CEO Hock Tan questioned whether investors understand what they own.

Barclays estimates current AI-related revenue at about $250B against more than $1T needed to sustain maintenance capex. AI-capex beneficiaries are expected to drive the majority of S&P 500 profit growth next year, and semiconductors roughly 60%.
BofA survey: 45% of investors expect an AI bubble in 2027 and 39% see hyperscaler capex as the most likely source of a systemic credit event.
KOSPI fell sharply as chipmakers sold off after Broadcom CEO's comments. Semis are breaking down on worries about Chinese alternatives pressuring margins and about capex.

AAPL joined NVDA in the $5 trillion market cap club. Cyclicals lagged defensives in 6 of the last 7 days. Quality outperformed momentum by about 30% over 3 months, the largest spread since 2020 per Goldman's Lee Coppersmith. Momentum kept sliding.

Big-bank earnings: Citi fell sharply, Goldman outperformed, JPM was unchanged. Goldman traders said early financials weakness likely reflected financials acting as a funding short for AI-trade weakness.
Goldman flows were balanced: long-only funds were net sellers, mainly info tech and macro products, and hedge funds were 9% better buyers, mainly info tech and communication services.

Nasdaq gamma has flipped negative per MenthorQ, so dealer hedging amplifies moves. SPX remains buffered by positive gamma between 7,700 and 7,800, making 7,700 the key level. A break could turn an AI-trade drawdown into a broader correction.

The median S&P 500 stock is well below its recent high and only 2 of 11 sectors are outperforming the index. Healthcare and financials strength hints at rotation, but no clear leadership replacement exists.

DXY held near its highest level since May 2025. Bloomberg's Monkam says the dollar is shifting back toward a monetary-policy-divergence trade as the 2-year UST-Bund spread widens on the Fed's hawkish repricing.
Gold gained overnight on a softer dollar but gave it back as oil rallied and yields rose. Bitcoin swung over 48 hours between debasement and high-beta tech regimes.

BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky sees an 'uncanny' analog between semis now and semis at the top of the dotcom bubble. If it holds, semis would low within 24 hours, rally once more, then sell off harder later in October.

tension_points.bear_case: The economics of the marginal project are weakening: lenders want less exposure, spreads are wider, and higher yields raise the hurdle for AI investment.
